root_cause.text: In the i915 DSI timing calculation code, DSC horizontal timing compensation was incorrectly applied in command mode as well as video mode, causing htotal to be reduced too far and leading to a zero line_time_us/div-by-zero when computing vtotal.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `gen11_dsi_set_transcoder_timings()` and `gen11_dsi_get_timings()` in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/icl_dsi.c` from checking only `crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable` / `pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16` to requiring `is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) && ...`, and the commit message explicitly says to “Stop adjusting the horizontal timing values based on the compression ratio in command mode” because the adjusted `htotal` becomes so small that `line_time_us==0` “when trying to determine the vtotal value in command mode.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict DSC timing adjustment to video mode DSI links.
intent_record.what: The conditional in gen11_dsi_set_transcoder_timings() was changed from checking only crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable to additionally requiring is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) to be true before applying the DSC-based mul/div calculation.
intent_record.how: DSC compression scaling is now applied only for video mode DSI links, preventing the compressed-bpp timing adjustment from being used in non-video modes.

intent_record.intent_summary: Restrict DSC timing adjustment to video mode DSI paths to avoid applying it in unsupported cases.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the DSC-related timing adjustment in gen11_dsi_get_timings() was changed from checking only pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16 to checking both is_vid_mode(intel_dsi) and pipe_config->dsc.compressed_bpp_x16.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the compressed-bpp timing adjustment will now run only for video mode DSI links that also have DSC compression enabled, preventing this calculation from being applied in non-video mode cases where it may be inappropriate.

grouping_result.intent: Restrict DSC timing adjustment to video mode DSI paths to avoid applying it in unsupported cases.

consistency_review.core_intent: Restrict DSC timing adjustment to video mode DSI links to avoid applying it in unsupported cases.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it restricts DSC horizontal timing compensation to video mode only, preventing it from being incorrectly applied in command mode and avoiding the htotal/line_time_us divide-by-zero issue.

candidates.rationale: This condition applies DSC timing compensation whenever compression is enabled, without restricting it to video mode. That allows the horizontal timing adjustment to run in command mode too, which can over-reduce htotal and trigger the zero line_time_us/div-by-zero failure.

This condition unconditionally enables DSC-based timing adjustment whenever compressed_bpp_x16 is set, rather than limiting it to video mode DSI. In command mode this can incorrectly shrink htotal too far and lead to invalid vtotal calculation.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present: horizontal timings are always scaled when DSC is enabled, regardless of mode. The code says, "if (crtc_state->dsc.compression_enable) { mul = crtc_state->dsc.compressed_bpp; div = mipi_dsi_pixel_format_to_bpp(intel_dsi->pixel_format); }" and then applies that to "htotal = DIV_ROUND_UP(adjusted_mode->crtc_htotal * mul, div);" and "hsync_start = DIV_ROUND_UP(...)." There is no check restricting this compensation to video mode only. The snippet later notes "TRANS_HSYNC register to be programmed only for video mode" but the DSC horizontal compensation has already been applied before that, so command mode is still affected. The fix is not present in this body because there is no gating like "if (intel_dsi->operation_mode == INTEL_DSI_VIDEO_MODE)" around the DSC timing adjustment.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is DSC horizontal timing compensation being applied in command mode, which would reduce htotal too far and trigger bad vtotal/line_time_us math. This function does not contain any DSC compensation logic at all. The only horizontal adjustment here is dual-link handling: `if (intel_dsi->dual_link) { hactive /= 2; ... htotal /= 2; }` and later programming `HTOTAL(dsi_trans)` with `(hactive - 1) | ((htotal - 1) << 16)`. There is no code that applies DSC-specific horizontal timing compensation, nor any sign of the incorrect command-mode application from the root cause. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent, and the fix is effectively already present in the sense that this function does not exhibit the bug.
